idea-plugin.name: Clotr
idea-plugin.description:
Clotr flags credentials in open files as you edit. Credential checks are on by default. Checks for personal details in open files start off and can be turned on in settings.

Use Check my clipboard or Check selection before sharing text. Clotr checks up to 1 MB of text and can copy a cleaned version with Bandage placeholders.

Set up Clotr Guard from Tools or Clotr settings when you want to check prompts and file reads in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI or Windsurf. Guard setup needs Node.js, previews its changes and waits for your approval.

The plugin runs in the IDE and makes no network calls. It reads .clotrignore at the repository root. Secret files stay silent in the editor. If Git does not ignore a secret file, Clotr shows one project note with an option to add it to .gitignore.

Free and open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Source and issues.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Two known issues. A path under a camelCase setting like authToken gets a password warning, and so does a plain number after a login code and "and".
  • The newer engine finds passwords under camelCase names like dbPassword: in YAML, JSON and XML, tokens in 19 more formats, secret webhook links, and a password inside an ssh:// or other login link.
  • Stand-in keys and passwords, a key block of only "...", a key file's path, a setting in backticks like `secret: true` and an order number shaped like a card no longer raise a warning.
  • Check my clipboard and Check selection show dots for a password or private key, and two characters at each end of a key at most.
  • When one of those checks runs out of time, Copy a cleaned version checks the rest of the text first and copies nothing if it can't finish.
  • A file of thousands of blank lines is checked in under half a second, where 0.1.2 took up to 91 seconds.
  • The icon has the same steel corner disc as the VS Code extension. The source is regrouped into readable files, with no change in how the plugin works.
